<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>


<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 0"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 0.25in"><B>1.</B></TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify"><B><A NAME="sp2a_009"></A>CORPORATE INFORMATION</B></TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">Banco Macro SA (hereinafter, the &ldquo;Bank&rdquo;)
is a business corporation (<I>sociedad an&oacute;nima</I>) organized in the Argentine Republic that offers traditional banking products
and services to companies, including those companies operating in regional economies as well as to individuals, thus strengthening its
goal to be a multiservice bank. In addition, through its subsidiaries, the Bank performs transactions as a trustee agent, manager and
administrator of mutual funds and renders stock exchange services, electronic payment services and granting of guarantees.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">Macro Compa&ntilde;&iacute;a Financiera
SA was created in 1977, as a non-banking financial institution. In May&nbsp;1988, it received the authorization to operate as a commercial
bank and was incorporated as Banco Macro SA. Subsequently, as a result of the merger process with other entities, it adopted other names
(among them, Banco Macro Bansud SA) and since August&nbsp;2006, Banco Macro SA.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">The Bank&rsquo;s shares are publicly
listed on Bolsas y Mercados Argentinos (BYMA, for its acronym in Spanish) since November&nbsp;1994 and as from March&nbsp;24, 2006 they
are listed on the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE). Additionally, on October&nbsp;15, 2015, they were authorized to be listed on A3 Mercados
SA (former Mercado Abierto Electr&oacute;nico SA (MAE, for its acronym in Spanish)).</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">Since 1994, Banco Macro SA&rsquo;s
market strategy has mainly focused on the regional areas outside the Autonomous City of Buenos Aires (CABA, for its acronym in Spanish).
Following this strategy, in 1996, Banco Macro SA started the process to acquire entities and assets and liabilities during the privatization
of provincial banks and other banking institutions.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">On May&nbsp;18, 2023, Banco Macro
SA acquired 100% of the capital stock of Macro Agro SAU (formerly known as Comercio Interior SAU). The main purpose of this company is
grain brokerage. For further information see also Note 11.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">Additionally, on November&nbsp;2,
2023, the Board of Directors of the Central Bank of Argentina (BCRA, for its acronym in Spanish), authorized the acquisition by Banco
Macro SA of 100% of the capital stock of Banco Ita&uacute; Argentina SA,&nbsp;Ita&uacute; Asset Management SA and Ita&uacute; Valores
SA.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">On January&nbsp;1, 2025, Banco Macro
SA acquired the control of Alianza SGR. The main purpose of this company is the granting of guarantees.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">On November&nbsp;26, 2025, the Board
of Directors approved the issuance of these condensed consolidated interim Financial Statements.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 0"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 0.25in"><B>2.</B></TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify"><B><A NAME="sp2a_010"></A>OPERATIONS OF THE BANK</B></TD></TR></TABLE>

<TD STYLE="width: 0.25in"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 0.25in">2.1</TD><TD><U>Agreement with the Misiones Provincial Government</U></TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify">The Bank and the Misiones Provincial
Government entered into a special-relationship agreement whereby the Bank was appointed, for a five-year term since January&nbsp;1, 1996,
as the Provincial Government&rsquo;s exclusive financial agent as well as revenue collection and obligation payment agent.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify">On November&nbsp;25, 1999, December&nbsp;28,
2006 and October&nbsp;1, 2018, extensions to such agreement were agreed upon, making it currently effective through December&nbsp;31,
2029.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify">As of September&nbsp;30, 2025 and December&nbsp;31,
2024, the deposits held by the Misiones Provincial Government with the Bank amounted to 72,842,619 and 118,494,050 (including 18,434,238
and 15,139,358 related to court deposits), respectively.</P>

de Tucum&aacute;n and the Municipality of Yerba Buena. The services agreements with the Provincial and Municipal Governments are effective

of San Miguel de Tucum&aacute;n was extended until 2028.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify">As of September&nbsp;30, 2025 and December&nbsp;31,
2024, the deposits held by the Tucum&aacute;n Provincial Government, the Municipality of San Miguel de Tucum&aacute;n and the Municipality
of Yerba Buena with the Bank amounted to 366,385,606 and 400,460,623 (including 59,759,627 and 51,483,686, related to court deposits),
respectively.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify">Additionally, the Bank granted loans
to the Tucum&aacute;n Provincial Government and the Municipalities of San Miguel de Tucum&aacute;n and Yerba Buena as of September&nbsp;30,
2025 and December&nbsp;31, 2024 for an amount of 81,102,898 and 71,615, respectively.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 0"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 0.25in"><B>3.</B></TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify"><B><A NAME="sp2a_011"></A>BASIS FOR THE PREPARATION OF THESE
                                            FINANCIAL STATEMENTS AND APPLICABLE ACCOUNTING STANDARDS</B></TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify"><B><U>Presentation basis</U></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify"><U>Applicable Accounting Standards</U></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">These condensed consolidated interim
Financial Statements of the Bank were prepared in accordance with the accounting framework established by the BCRA, in its Communiqu&eacute;
 &ldquo;A&rdquo; 6114 as supplemented. Except for the regulatory provisions established by the BCRA, which are explained in the following
paragraph, such framework is based on IFRS Accounting Standards (International Financial Reporting Standards) as issued by the IASB (International
Accounting Standards Board) and adopted by the Argentine Federation of Professionals Councils in Economic Sciences (FACPCE, for its acronym
in Spanish). The abovementioned international standards include the International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS), the International
Accounting Standards (IAS) and the interpretations developed by the IFRS Interpretations Committee (IFRIC) or former Standing Interpretations
Committee (SIC).</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"></P>

    <DIV STYLE="margin-top: 12pt; margin-bottom: 6pt; border-bottom: Black 1pt solid"><P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: center; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><!-- Field: Sequence; Type: Arabic; Name: PageNo -->10<!-- Field: /Sequence --></P></DIV>
    <DIV STYLE="break-before: page; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 12pt"><P STYLE="margin: 0pt">&nbsp;</P></DIV>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center"><B>NOTES TO THE CONDENSED CONSOLIDATED INTERIM
FINANCIAL STATEMENTS&nbsp;</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center"><B>AS OF SEPTEMBER 30, 2025</B>&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center">(Translation of Financial Statements originally
issued in Spanish &ndash; See Note 44)&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center">(Figures stated in thousands of pesos in constant
currency)</P>


<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">The transitory exceptions established
by BCRA to the application of effective IFRS Accounting Standards as issued by the IASB that affect the preparation of these condensed
consolidated interim Financial Statements are as follows:</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 0.25in"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 0.25in">a)</TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify">According to Communiqu&eacute; &ldquo;A&rdquo;
                                            6114, as amended and supplemented, and in the convergence process through IFRS Accounting
                                            Standards as issued by the IASB, the BCRA established that since fiscal years beginning on
                                            or after January&nbsp;1, 2020, financial institutions defined as &ldquo;Group A&rdquo; by
                                            BCRA rules, in which the Bank is included, begin to apply section 5.5 &ldquo;Impairment&rdquo;
                                            of the IFRS 9 &ldquo;Financial Instruments&rdquo; (sections B5.5.1 to B5.5.55), except for
                                            the temporary exclusion for the public sector established by Communiqu&eacute; &ldquo;A&rdquo;
                                            6847. As of the date of issuance of these condensed consolidated interim Financial Statements,
                                            the Bank is in the process of quantifying the effect of the full application of the abovementioned
                                            standard.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 0.25in"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 0.25in">b)</TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify">Through Communiqu&eacute; &ldquo;A&rdquo;
                                            7014 dated May&nbsp;14, 2020, the BCRA established for financial institutions that received
                                            debt securities of the public sector in a swap transaction, they must be initially recognized
                                            at their carrying amount as of the date of the swap transaction, without assessing if they
                                            qualify or not for derecognition under IFRS 9 standards and as a consequence, do not eventually
                                            recognize the new instruments at the market value as provided by such IFRS (see Note 9 to
                                            the condensed consolidated interim Financial Statements).</TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify">If IFRS 9 had been applied, according
to an estimation calculated by the Bank, the Statement of income of the nine-month period ended September&nbsp;30, 2025, would have recorded
an increase in &ldquo;Interest income&rdquo; for an amount of 99,375, in &ldquo;Loss on net monetary position&rdquo; for an amount of
29,203 and in &ldquo;Income tax on continuing operations&rdquo; for an amount of 64,519 and, on the other hand, a decrease in &ldquo;Net
gain from measurement of financial instruments at fair value through profit or loss&rdquo; for an amount of 238,718, and as a counterpart
an increase in &ldquo;Other comprehensive income&rdquo; for that period. In addition, it would have been recorded in the Statement of
income of the nine-month period ended September&nbsp;30, 2024 an increase in &ldquo;Interest income&rdquo; for an amount of 3,364, in
 &ldquo;Loss on net monetary position&rdquo; for an amount of 2,745 and in &ldquo;Net gain from measurement of financial instruments at
fair value through profit or loss&rdquo; for an amount of 115,364, and as a counterpart an increase in &ldquo;Other comprehensive income&rdquo;
for that period. These changes would not have resulted into modifications to the total shareholder equity as of those dates or the total
comprehensive income of the nine-month periods ended September&nbsp;30, 2025 and 2024.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">Except for what was mentioned in the
previous paragraphs, the accounting policies applied by the Bank comply with the IFRS Accounting Standards as issued by the IASB as currently
approved and are applicable to the preparation of these condensed consolidated interim Financial Statements in accordance with the IFRS
Accounting Standards as issued by the IASB and adopted by the BCRA through Communiqu&eacute; &ldquo;A&rdquo; 8164. Generally, the BCRA
does not allow the anticipated application of any IFRS Accounting Standards, unless otherwise expressly stated.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify"><U>Basis for preparation and consolidation</U></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">These condensed consolidated interim
Financial Statements as of September&nbsp;30, 2025, have been prepared in accordance with the accounting framework established by the
BCRA as mentioned in the previous section &ldquo;Applicable accounting standards&rdquo; which, particularly for condensed consolidated
interim Financial Statements, is based on IAS 34 &ldquo;Interim Financial Reporting&rdquo;.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">For the preparation of these condensed
consolidated interim Financial Statements, in addition to section &ldquo;Measuring unit&rdquo; of this note, the Bank has applied the
basis for the preparation and consolidation, the accounting policies and the material accounting judgments, estimates and assumptions
described in the consolidated Financial Statements for the fiscal year ended on December&nbsp;31, 2024, already issued.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">These condensed consolidated interim
Financial Statements include all the necessary information for an appropriate understanding, by the users thereof, of the basis for the
preparation and disclosure used therein as well as the relevant events and transactions occurred after the issuance of the last annual
consolidated Financial Statements for the fiscal year ended on December&nbsp;31, 2024, already issued. Nevertheless, the present condensed
consolidated interim Financial Statements do not include all the information or all the disclosures required for the annual consolidated
Financial Statements prepared in accordance with the IAS 1 &ldquo;Presentation of Financial Statements&rdquo;. Therefore, these condensed
consolidated interim Financial Statements must be read together with the annual consolidated Financial Statements for the fiscal year
ended December&nbsp;31, 2024, already issued.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify"><U>Going concern</U></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">The Bank&rsquo;s management has made
an assessment of its ability to continue as a going concern and concluded that it has the resources to continue in business for the foreseeable
future. Furthermore, management is not aware of any material uncertainties that may cast significant doubt on the Bank&rsquo;s ability
to continue as a going concern. Therefore, these condensed consolidated interim Financial Statements were prepared on a going concern
basis.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify"><U>Transcription into books</U></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">As of the date of issuance of these
condensed consolidated interim Financial Statements, they are in the process of being transcribed into the Financial Statements book
(&ldquo;Libro Balances&rdquo;) of Banco Macro SA.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify"><U>Figures stated in thousands of
pesos</U></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">These condensed consolidated interim
Financial Statements disclose figures stated in thousands of argentine pesos in terms of purchasing power as of September&nbsp;30, 2025,
and are rounded up to the nearest amount in thousands of pesos, except as otherwise indicated (see section &ldquo;Measuring unit&rdquo;
of this note).</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">The condensed consolidated interim
statement of financial position as of September&nbsp;30, 2025, is presented comparatively with year-end data of the immediately preceding

information have been restated to consider the changes in the general purchasing power of the functional currency and, as a result, are

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">Additionally, as it is mentioned in

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center"><B>NOTES TO THE CONDENSED CONSOLIDATED INTERIM
FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</B>&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center"><B>AS OF SEPTEMBER 30, 2025</B>&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center">(Translation of Financial Statements originally
issued in Spanish &ndash; See Note 44)</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center">(Figures stated in thousands of pesos in constant
currency)</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify"><U>Measuring unit</U></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">These condensed consolidated interim
Financial Statements have been restated for the changes in the general purchasing power of the functional currency (argentine pesos)
as of September&nbsp;30, 2025, as established by IAS 29 &ldquo;Financial Reporting in Hyperinflationary Economies&rdquo; and considering,
in addition, specific rules&nbsp;established by BCRA through Communiqu&eacute;s &ldquo;A&rdquo; 6651, 6849, as amended and supplemented,
which established the obligation to apply this method, from fiscal years beginning on or after January&nbsp;1, 2020, and determined as
the transition date December&nbsp;31, 2018.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">According to IFRS Accounting Standards
as issued by the IASB, the restatement of Financial Statements is needed when the functional currency is the currency of a hyperinflationary
economy. To achieve consistency in identifying an economic environment of that nature,&nbsp;IAS 29 establishes (i)&nbsp;certain nonexclusive
qualitative indicators, consisting in analyzing the general population behavior, prices, interest rates and wages with changes in price
indexes and the loss of purchasing power, and (ii)&nbsp;as quantitative characteristic, which is the most used condition in practice,
to test if a three-year cumulative inflation rate is around 100% or more. Due to miscellaneous macroeconomic factors, the three-year
inflation rate exceeded that figure and the Argentine government goals and other available estimates also indicate that this trend will
not be reversed in the short term.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">The restatement must be applied as
if the economy had always been hyperinflationary, using a general price index that reflects changes in general purchasing power. To apply
the restatement, a series of indexes are used, as prepared and published on a monthly basis by the FACPCE, which combines the consumer
price index (CPI) on a monthly basis published by the Argentine Institute of Statistics and Censuses (INDEC, for its acronym in Spanish)
since January&nbsp;2017 (baseline month: December&nbsp;2016) with the wholesale prices index (WPI) published by the INDEC until that
date. For the months of November&nbsp;and December&nbsp;2015, for which the INDEC did not publish the WPI variation, the CPI variation
for CABA was used.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">Considering the abovementioned indexes,
the inflation rate was 21.97% and 101.58% for the nine-month periods ended on September&nbsp;30, 2025 and 2024, respectively, and 117.76%
for the fiscal year ended on December&nbsp;31, 2024.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">Below is a description of the restatement
mechanism provided by IAS 29 &ldquo;Financial Reporting in Hyperinflationary Economies&rdquo; and the restatement process for Financial
Statements established by BCRA Communiqu&eacute; &ldquo;A&rdquo; 6849, as supplemented.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify"><U>Description of the main aspects
of the restatement process for statements of financial position</U></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 0.25in"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 0.25in">(i)</TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify">Monetary items (those with a fixed nominal
                                            value in local currency) are not restated because they are already expressed in the current
                                            measuring unit as of the end of the reporting period. In an inflationary period, an entity
                                            holding monetary assets generates purchasing power loss and holding monetary liabilities
                                            generates purchasing power gain, provided that the assets and liabilities are not linked
                                            to an adjustment mechanism that offsets to some extent those effects. Net gain or loss on
                                            a monetary basis is included in profit or loss for the reporting period.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 0.25in"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 0.25in">(ii)</TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify">Assets and liabilities subject to adjustments
                                            based on specific agreements are adjusted in accordance with such agreements.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 0.25in"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 0.25in">(iii)</TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify">Non-monetary items stated at current
                                            cost at the end of the reporting period, are not restated for presentation purposes in the
                                            statement of financial position, but the adjustment process must be completed to determine,
                                            in terms of constant measuring unit, the profit or loss produced by holding these non-monetary
                                            items.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 0.25in"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 0.25in">(iv)</TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify">Non-monetary items carried at historical
                                            cost or at current cost at some earlier date before the reporting date, are restated at indexes
                                            that reflects the general level of price variation from the acquisition or revaluation date
                                            to the closing date, proceeding then to compare the restated amounts of those assets with
                                            their recoverable amounts. Profit or loss of the period related to depreciation of property,
                                            plant and equipment and amortization of intangible assets, as well as any other non-monetary
                                            assets cost are determined on the basis of the new restated amounts.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 0.25in"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 0.25in">(v)</TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify">When an entity capitalizes borrowing
                                            cost in the non-monetary assets, the part of the borrowing cost that compensates the creditor
                                            for the effects of inflation is not capitalized.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 0.25in"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 0.25in">(vi)</TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify">The restatement of non-monetary assets
                                            in terms of a current measuring unit at the end of the reporting period, without an equivalent
                                            adjustment for tax purposes results in a taxable temporary difference and the recognition
                                            of deferred income tax liability whose balancing entry is recognized in profit or loss of
                                            the period. When, beyond the restatement, there is a revaluation of non-monetary assets,
                                            the deferred tax related to the restatement is recognized in profit or loss of the period
                                            and deferred tax related to the revaluation (surplus of the revalued value over the restated
                                            value) is recognized in other comprehensive income.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center"><B>NOTES TO THE CONDENSED CONSOLIDATED INTERIM
FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</B>&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center"><B>AS OF SEPTEMBER 30, 2025</B>&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center">(Translation of Financial Statements originally
issued in Spanish &ndash; See Note 44)&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center">(Figures stated in thousands of pesos in constant
currency)</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify"><U>Description of the main aspects
of the restatement process for statements of income and other comprehensive income</U></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 0.25in"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 0.25in">(i)</TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify">Expenses and income are restated from
                                            the date the items were recorded, except for those profit or loss items that reflect or include,
                                            in their determination, the consumption of assets measured at purchasing power currency of
                                            a date prior to that which the consumption was recorded, which are restated using as basis
                                            the origination date of the assets related to the item; and also except for income or loss
                                            arising from comparing two measurements at purchasing power currency of different dates,
                                            for which it requires to identify the amounts compared, restate them separately and repeat
                                            the comparison, with the amounts already restated.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 0.25in"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 0.25in">(ii)</TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify">Gain or loss on monetary position will
                                            be classified based on the item that generated it and is presented in a separate line reflecting
                                            effect of inflation on monetary items.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify"><U>Description of the main aspects
of the restatement process for the statements of changes in shareholders&rsquo; equity</U></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in"><B><U>Accounting judgments, estimates and assumptions</U></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">The preparation of these condensed
consolidated interim Financial Statements requires the Bank&rsquo;s Management to consider significant accounting judgments, estimates
and assumptions that impact on the reported assets and liabilities, income and expenses, as well as the determination and disclosure
of contingent assets and liabilities, as of the end of the period. The Bank&rsquo;s reported amounts are based on the best estimate regarding
the probability of occurrence of different future events. Therefore, the uncertainties associated with the estimates and assumptions
adopted may drive in the future to final amounts that may differ from those estimates and may require significant adjustments to the
reported amounts of the affected assets and liabilities.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">The Bank applies the same accounting
judgments, estimates and assumptions described in Note 3 section &ldquo;Accounting judgments, estimates and assumptions&rdquo; to the
consolidated Financial Statements as of December&nbsp;31, 2024, already issued.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">For the fiscal year beginning on January&nbsp;1,

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify"><U>Amendments to IAS 21 - Lack of
exchangeability</U></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">In August&nbsp;2023, the IASB issued
amendments to IAS 21 related to &ldquo;Lack of exchangeability&rdquo;. The amendment to IAS 21 specifies how an entity should assess
whether a currency is exchangeable and how it should determine a spot exchange rate when exchangeability is lacking. A currency is considered
to be exchangeable into another currency when an entity is able to obtain the other currency within a time frame that allows for a normal
administrative delay and through a market or exchange mechanism in which an exchange transaction would create enforceable rights and
obligations. If a currency is not exchangeable into another currency, an entity is required to estimate the spot exchange rate at the
measurement date. An entity&rsquo;s objective in estimating the spot exchange rate is to reflect the rate at which an orderly exchange
transaction would take place at the measurement date between market participants under prevailing economic conditions. The amendments
state that an entity may use an unadjusted observable exchange rate or other estimation technique.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">When an entity estimates a spot exchange
rate because a currency is not exchangeable into another currency, it will disclose information that enables users of the financial statements
to understand how the currency not being exchangeable into another currency affects, or is expected to affect, the entity's performance,
financial position and cash flows. This amendment did not have a material impact on the condensed consolidated interim Financial Statements.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify"><B><U>New pronouncements</U></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">Pursuant to Communiqu&eacute; &ldquo;A&rdquo;
6114 of the BCRA, as new IFRS Accounting Standards as issued by the IASB are approved and existing IFRS Accounting Standards are amended
or revoked and once these changes are approved through the notices of approval issued by the FACPCE, the BCRA shall issue a statement
on the approval thereof for financial entities. Generally, financial institutions shall not apply any IFRS in advance, except as specifically
authorized at the time of the adoption thereof.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">The new and amended standards and
interpretations that are issued, but not yet effective, up to the date of issuance of these condensed consolidated interim Financial
Statements are disclosed below. The Bank intends to adopt these standards, if applicable, when they become effective:</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify"><U>IFRS 18 &ndash; Presentation and
disclosure in Financial Statements</U></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">In April&nbsp;2024, the IASB issued
IFRS 18, &ldquo;Presentation and disclosure in Financial Statements&rdquo;, which addresses the format for the presentation of profit
or loss in the Financial Statements, management-defined performance measures and aggregation/disaggregation of disclosures information.
This standard will replace IAS 1 and is effective as of January&nbsp;1, 2027. The Bank is evaluating the effects that this standard would
cause on the condensed consolidated interim Financial Statements.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

needs of customers, the Bank&rsquo;s credit policy also includes, among others, the granting of guarantees, securities, bonds, letters

financial position and, therefore, they are an integral part of the total risk of the Bank.</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 0"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 0.25in"><B>8.</B></TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify"><B>LOSS ALLOWANCE FOR EXPECTED CREDIT
                                            LOSSES ON CREDIT EXPOSURES NOT MEASURED AT FAIR VALUE THROUGH PROFIT OR LOSS</B></TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">The Bank recognizes a loss allowance
for expected credit losses on all credit exposures not measured at fair value through profit or loss, like debt instruments measured
at amortized cost, debt instruments measured at fair value through other comprehensive income, loan commitments and financial guarantee
contracts (not measured at fair value through profit or loss), contract assets and lease receivables.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">Note 10 discloses financial assets
measured at fair value on a recurring basis and financial assets not recognized at fair value. This classification is made pursuant to
the expressed in Note 3 &ldquo;Basis for the preparation of these Financial Statements and applicable accounting standards&rdquo; to
the consolidated Financial Statements as of December&nbsp;31, 2024, already issued. Additionally, Note 10 explains the information related
to the valuation process.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">Moreover, considering the temporary
exclusion established by BCRA mentioned in Note 3 &ldquo;Applicable accounting standards&rdquo; the Bank applies the impairment requirements
for the recognition and measurement of a loss allowance for financial assets measured at amortized cost or at fair value through other
comprehensive income, except for public sector exposures. In addition, the Bank applies the impairment requirements for guarantees granted,
undrawn commitments of credit cards, checking account advance agreements and letters of credit, which are not recognized in the condensed
consolidated interim Statement of financial position.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

credit risk exposure and identifying material credit risk concentration, disclosures regarding credit risk of financial assets and off
balance items are as follows.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center"><B>NOTES TO THE CONDENSED CONSOLIDATED INTERIM
FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</B>&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center"><B>AS OF SEPTEMBER 30, 2025</B>&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center">(Translation of Financial Statements originally
issued in Spanish &ndash; See Note 44)</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center">(Figures stated in thousands of pesos in constant
currency)</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify">The Bank resolved to establish an allowance
based on expert judgment, making an estimate that considers the effects of covering a scenario of uncertainty as a result of implementing
the macroeconomic imbalances adjustment program and the inflation stabilization plan. As of September&nbsp;30, 2025, this adjustment
was estimated at 37,480,326.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

quality and the carrying amount of credit risk, based on the Bank&rsquo;s credit risk rating system, the probability of default (PD)
and the year-end stage classification, taking into account what was mentioned in the previous paragraph. The amounts are presented gross
of the impairment allowances.</P>

<TD STYLE="width: 0.25in"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 0.25in">8.2</TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify">Other debt securities at amortized cost</TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify">The criterion used to calculate ECL
of Financial Trusts and Corporate Bonds is based on the rating granted by risk rating agencies to each debt security type making up each
financial trust or each corporate bond series, respectively. This means that the factor to be used will vary depending on the debt securities
holdings (A or B). The exposure at default (EAD) is assumed to be equal to the outstanding balance.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-align: justify; text-indent: -0.25in">The table below

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 0"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 0.25in"><B>10.</B></TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify"><B>FAIR VALUE QUANTITATIVE AND QUALITATIVE
                                            DISCLOSURES</B></TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">The fair value is the amount at which
an asset can be exchanged, or at which a liability can be settled, in mutual independent terms and conditions between participants of
the principal market (or the most advantageous market) who are duly informed and willing to transact in an orderly and current transaction,
at the measurement date under the current market conditions whether the price is directly observable or estimated using a valuation technique
under the assumption that the Bank is an ongoing business.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">When a financial instrument is quoted
in a liquid and active market, its price in the market in a real transaction provides the most reliable evidence of its fair value. Nevertheless,
when there is no quoted price in the market or it cannot be evidence of the fair value of such instrument, in order to determine such
fair value, the entities may use the market value of another instrument with similar characteristics, the analysis of discounted cash
flows or other applicable techniques, which shall be significantly affected by the assumptions used.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">Although the Bank&rsquo;s Management
has used its best judgment to estimate the fair values of its financial instruments, any technique to perform such estimate implies certain
inherent fragility level.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center"><B>AS OF SEPTEMBER 30, 2025</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in"><U>Fair value hierarchy</U></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">The Bank uses the following hierarchy
to determine and disclose the fair value of financial instruments, according to the valuation technique applied:</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 18pt"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 17.45pt">-</TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify">Level 1: quoted prices (unadjusted) observable
                                            in active markets that the Bank accesses to at the measurement day for identical assets or
                                            liabilities. The Bank considers markets as active only if there are sufficient trading activities
                                            with respect to the volume and liquidity of the identical assets or liabilities and when
                                            there are binding and exercisable price quotes available at the end of each period or fiscal
                                            year, as applicable.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 18pt"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 17.45pt">-</TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify">Level 2: Valuation techniques for which
                                            the data and variables having a significant impact on the determination of the fair value
                                            recognized or disclosed are observable for the asset or liability, either directly or indirectly.
                                            Such inputs include quoted prices for similar assets or liabilities in active markets, quoted
                                            prices for identical instruments in inactive markets and observable inputs other than quoted
                                            prices, such as interest rates and yield curves, implied volatilities, and credit spreads.
                                            In addition, adjustments to level 2 inputs may be required for the condition or location
                                            of the asset or the extent to which it relates to items that are comparable to the valued
                                            instrument. However, if such adjustments are based on unobservable inputs that are significant
                                            to the entire measurement, the Bank will classify the instruments as Level 3.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 18pt"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 17.45pt">-</TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify">Level 3: Valuation techniques for which
                                            the data and variables having a significant impact on the determination of the fair value
                                            recognized or disclosed are not based on observable market information.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">The following tables show the hierarchy
in the Bank&rsquo;s financial asset and liability at fair value measurement on a recurring basis, as of September&nbsp;30, 2025 and December&nbsp;31,
2024:</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.25in"><U>Description of the valuation
process</U></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">The fair value of instruments categorized
as level 1 was assessed by using quoted prices effective at the end of each period or fiscal year, as applicable, in active markets for
identical assets or liabilities, if representative. Currently, for most of the government and private securities, there are two principal
markets in which the Bank operates: BYMA and A3 Mercados SA (former Mercado Abierto Electr&oacute;nico SA).</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">On the other hand, for certain assets
and liabilities that do not have an active market, categorized as level 2, the Bank used valuation techniques that included the use of
market transactions performed under mutual independent terms and conditions, between interested and duly informed parties, provided that
they are available as well as references to the current fair value of another instrument being substantially similar, or otherwise the
analysis of cash flows discounted at rates built from market information of similar instruments.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">In addition, certain assets and liabilities
included in this category were valued using price quotes of identical instruments in &ldquo;less active markets&rdquo;.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">Finally, the Bank has categorized
as level 3 those assets and liabilities for which there are no identical or similar transactions in the market. To determine the market
value of these instruments the Bank used valuation techniques based on own assumptions and independent appraisers&rsquo; valuations.
For this approach, the Bank mainly used the cash flow discount model.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">As of September&nbsp;30, 2025 and
December&nbsp;31, 2024, the Bank has neither changed the techniques nor the assumptions used to estimate the fair value of the financial
instruments.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"></P>

    <TD STYLE="border-bottom: Black 1pt solid; font: bold 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: left">&nbsp;</TD><TD STYLE="border-bottom: Black 1pt solid; font: bold 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: right">225,827</TD><TD STYLE="padding-bottom: 1pt; font: bold 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: left">&nbsp;</TD><TD STYLE="font: bold 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; padding-bottom: 1pt">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD STYLE="border-bottom: Black 1pt solid; font: bold 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: left">&nbsp;</TD><TD STYLE="border-bottom: Black 1pt solid; font: bold 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: right">8,040,496</TD><TD STYLE="padding-bottom: 1pt; font: bold 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: left">&nbsp;</TD></TR>
  </TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">The fair values of instruments measured
at level 3 are determined by the Bank based on valuation techniques derived from the &quot;income method&quot;, whose main unobservable
data are related to discount rates, and on which a reasonable change in such input data would not generate significant effects on the
Financial Statements taken as a whole.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify"><U>Changes in fair value levels</U></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">The Bank monitors the availability
of information in the market to evaluate the classification of financial instruments into the fair value hierarchy as well as the resulting
determination of transfers between levels 1, 2 and 3 at each period end.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">Except for the foregoing, as of September&nbsp;30,
2025 and December&nbsp;31, 2024, the Bank has not recognized any transfers between levels 1, 2 and 3.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify"><U>Financial assets and liabilities
not measured at fair value</U></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">Next follows a description of the
main methods and assumptions used to determine the fair values of financial instruments not recognized at their fair value in these condensed
consolidated interim Financial Statements:</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 18pt"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 17.45pt">-</TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify">Instruments with fair value similar to
                                            the carrying amount: financial assets and liabilities that are liquid or have short-term
                                            maturities (less than three months) were deemed to have a fair value similar to the carrying
                                            amount.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 18pt"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 17.45pt">-</TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify">Fixed and variable rate of financial instruments:
                                            the fair value of financial assets was recognized discounting future cash flows at current
                                            market rates for each period or fiscal year, as applicable, for financial instruments of
                                            similar characteristics. The estimated fair value of fixed-interest rate deposits and liabilities
                                            was assessed discounting future cash flows by using estimated interest rates for deposits
                                            or placings with similar maturities to those of the Bank&rsquo;s portfolio.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 18pt"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 17.45pt">-</TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify">For public listed assets and liabilities,
                                            or those for which the prices are reported by certain renowned pricing providers, the fair
                                            value was determined based on such prices.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"></P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 0.25in"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 0.5in">11.1</TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify">Macro Agro SAU (formerly known as Comercio
                                            Interior SAU)</TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-align: justify">On May&nbsp;18, 2023, the Bank acquired
from Inversora Juramento SA, 100% of the capital stock and votes of Macro Agro SAU (formerly known as Comercio Interior SAU), a company
engaged in the grain brokerage business.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-align: justify">The Special Shareholders&rsquo; Meeting
held on October&nbsp;6, 2023 deemed it appropriate and approved the change of its corporate name to &ldquo;Macro Agro S.A.U.&rdquo; and,
consequently, subject to the authorization of the Business Associations Regulatory Agency of the Province of Santa Fe (IGPJ, for its
acronym in Spanish), proposed the amendment of section 1 of the by-laws. On October&nbsp;27, 2023, the proceedings were filed with the
IGPJ. Additionally, on March&nbsp;5, 2024, the Bank was notified of the resolution of the IGPJ, which approved the reform of the by-laws
with the name of Macro Agro SAU.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-align: justify"><U>Assets acquired and liabilities
assumed</U></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-align: justify">The goodwill generated by the acquisition
of Macro Agro SAU (formerly known as Comercio Interior SAU) amounted to 902,922.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-align: justify">In accordance with the share purchase
contract, the transaction price was set at USD 5,218,800, which will be paid in variable annual installments using the proceeds from
the dividends of Macro Agro SAU (formerly known as Comercio Interior SAU). Thus, the Bank assigns 100% of the rights over the dividends
in favor of the seller, up to the full payment of the purchase price. Each installment will become due within fifteen days as from the
Shareholders&rsquo; Meeting approval of the Financial Statements of Macro Agro SAU (formerly known as Comercio Interior SAU), starting
the first installment in 2024.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-align: justify">To measure the liabilities arising
from this transaction the Bank estimated the company's future income, discounting them at its own business rate. As a consequence, at
the acquisition date, the liability amounted to USD 2,973,375.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-align: justify">On September&nbsp;29, 2023, Macro
Agro SAU (formerly known as Comercio Interior SAU) distributed cash dividends amounting to 440,000 (not restated). Those dividends were
received by Banco Macro SA on October&nbsp;2, 2023. As a consequence of what was explained in the previous paragraphs, those dividends
were used to pay the liability arising from the purchase, which decreased by USD 558,651.70.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-align: justify">On April&nbsp;23, 2025, Macro Agro

Banco Macro SA on May&nbsp;5, 2025. As a consequence of what was explained in the previous paragraphs, those dividends were used to pay
the liability arising from the purchase, which decreased by USD 598,534.85.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-align: justify">Finally, on August&nbsp;21, 2025,
Macro Agro SAU (formerly known as Comercio Interior SAU) distributed cash dividends amounting to 544,000 (not restated), which were received
by Banco Macro SA on August&nbsp;27, 2025. As a consequence of what was explained in the previous paragraphs, those dividends were used
to pay the liability arising from the purchase, which decreased by USD 398,610.72.</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 0.25in"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 0.5in">11.2</TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify">Banco BMA SAU (formerly known as Banco
                                            Ita&uacute; Argentina SA) and its subsidiaries</TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-align: justify">On August&nbsp;23, 2023, Banco Macro
SA entered into a stock purchase agreement with Ita&uacute; Unibanco Holding SA, through its affiliates Ita&uacute; Unibanco SA, Banco
Ita&uacute; BBA SA and Ita&uacute; Consultoria de Valores Mobili&aacute;rios e Participa&ccedil;oes SA (collectively, &ldquo;Ita&uacute;&rdquo;),
pursuant to which, subject to certain conditions (substantially the approval of the transaction by the BCRA), the Bank would acquire
from Ita&uacute; the shares representing 100% of the capital stock and votes of Banco Ita&uacute; Argentina SA,&nbsp;Ita&uacute; Asset
Management SA and Ita&uacute; Valores SA.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-align: justify">On November&nbsp;2, 2023, the Board
of Directors of the BCRA authorized the abovementioned purchase, as per the following breakdown:</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">

                                            Ita&uacute; Argentina SA:</B> 100% of the capital stock and votes of Banco Ita&uacute; Argentina

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-align: justify">The price of this transaction was
established at USD 50,000,000, which was set at the time of the agreement and paid on November&nbsp;3, 2023, and an additional amount
resulting from the adjustment of the result obtained by Banco BMA SAU (formerly known as Banco Ita&uacute; Argentina SA), BMA Asset Management
SGFCISA (formerly known as Ita&uacute; Asset Management SA) and BMA Valores SA (formerly known as Ita&uacute; Valores SA) between April&nbsp;1,
2023 and the closing date established in the purchase contract, which was agreed between the parties in May&nbsp;2024 for an amount of
USD 7,564,706. The difference between such additional amount and the estimated additional amount at the acquisition date for an amount
of 14,050,768 was recorded in comparative information for prior year, presented in lines &ldquo;Other non-financial liabilities&rdquo;
and &ldquo;Loss from associates and joint ventures&rdquo; in accordance with IFRS 3, as it is explained in section &ldquo;Comparative
information&rdquo; of the Note 3.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-align: justify">Through Communiqu&eacute; &ldquo;C&rdquo;
99120, the BCRA informed that according to the authorization gave in due time through Resolution No.&nbsp;352 of the Board of Directors
dated October&nbsp;31, 2024, on November&nbsp;19, 2024, Banco Macro SA performed the merger by absorption of Banco BMA SAU. This merger
had in turn been resolved by the Shareholders' Meeting held on May&nbsp;6, 2024, with retroactive effect to January&nbsp;1, 2024, also
approved by the National Securities Commission (CNV, for its acronym in Spanish) on November&nbsp;6, 2024, and registered in the Public
Registry on November&nbsp;14, 2024. Therefore, since November&nbsp;19, 2024, the authorization of Banco BMA SAU to operate as a commercial
bank was revoked, and its buildings were incorporated to Banco Macro SA as branches.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">For management purposes, the Bank&rsquo;s
Management has determined that it has only one operating segment related to the banking business. In this sense, the Bank supervises the
operating segment income (loss) in order to make decisions about resources to be allocated to the segment and assess its performance,
which is measured on a consistent basis with the profit or loss in the Financial Statements.</P>

<TD STYLE="width: 0"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 0.25in"><B>21.</B></TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify"><B>INCOME TAX</B></TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 18pt"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 17.45pt">a)</TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify">Inflation adjustment on income tax</TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify">Tax Reform Law 27430, amended by Laws
27468 and 27541, established the following, regarding inflation adjustment on income tax for the fiscal years beginning on January&nbsp;1,
2018:</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 0.5in"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 0.25in">i)</TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify">such adjustment will be applicable in the fiscal year in which the variation of the CPI is higher than
100% for the thirty-six months before the end of the tax period;</TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 0.5in"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 0.25in">ii)</TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify">regarding the first, second and third fiscal year after its effective date, this procedure will be applicable
if the variation of the abovementioned index, calculated from the beginning until the end of each of those fiscal years exceeds 55%, 30%
and 15% for the first, second and third fiscal years of application, respectively;</TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 0.5in"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 0.25in">iii)</TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify">the positive or negative inflation adjustment, as the case may be, corresponding to the first, second
and third fiscal years beginning on January&nbsp;1, 2018, shall be allocated one third in the fiscal year for which the adjustment is
calculated and the remaining two thirds in equal parts in the following two immediate fiscal years;</TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 0.5in"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 0.25in">iv)</TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify">the positive or negative inflation adjustment, corresponding to the first and second fiscal years beginning
on January&nbsp;1, 2019, shall be allocated one sixth to the fiscal year in which the adjustment is determined and the remaining five
sixth in the following immediate fiscal years; and</TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 0.5in"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 0.25in">v)</TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify">for fiscal years beginning on January&nbsp;1, 2021, 100% of the adjustment may be deducted in the year
in which it is determined.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify">As of September&nbsp;30, 2025 and December&nbsp;31,
2024, all the conditions established by the income tax Law to practice the inflation adjustment are met (see section &ldquo;Fiscal years
2019 and 2020&rdquo; and &ldquo;Fiscal year 2021&rdquo; of this note).</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 18pt"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 17.45pt">b)</TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify">Corporate income tax rate</TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify">On June&nbsp;16, 2021, through Decree
No.&nbsp;387/2021, Law No.&nbsp;27630 was issued. This law established for fiscal years beginning on or after January&nbsp;1, 2021, a
progressive tax rates scheme of 25%, 30% and 35% which will be applied, on a progressive basis, to the taxable accumulated net profit
at the end of each fiscal year.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>
