<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center"><B>NOTES TO THE CONDENSED SEPARATE INTERIM FINANCIAL
STATEMENTS</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center"><B>AS OF SEPTEMBER 30, 2025</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center">(Translation of Financial Statements originally
issued in Spanish &ndash; See Note 41)</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center">(Figures stated in thousands of pesos in constant
currency)</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 0"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 0.25in"><B>1.</B></TD><TD><B>CORPORATE INFORMATION</B></TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">Banco Macro SA (hereinafter, the &ldquo;Bank&rdquo;)
is a business corporation (<I>sociedad an&oacute;nima</I>) organized in the Argentine Republic that offers traditional banking products
and services to companies, including those companies operating in regional economies as well as to individuals, thus strengthening its
goal to be a multiservice bank. In addition, the Bank performs certain transactions through its subsidiaries Macro Bank Limited (a company
organized under the laws of Bahamas), Macro Securities SAU, Macro Fiducia SAU, Macro Fondos SGFCISA, Argenpay SAU, Fintech SGR and Alianza
SGR.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">Macro Compa&ntilde;&iacute;a Financiera
SA was created in 1977 as a non-banking financial institution. In May&nbsp;1988, it received the authorization to operate as a commercial
bank and was incorporated as Banco Macro SA. Subsequently, as a result of the merger process with other entities, it adopted other names
(among them, Banco Macro Bansud SA) and since August&nbsp;2006, Banco Macro SA.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">The Bank&rsquo;s shares are publicly
listed on Bolsas y Mercados Argentinos (BYMA, for its acronym in Spanish) since November&nbsp;1994 and as from March&nbsp;24, 2006, they
are listed on the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE). Additionally, on October&nbsp;15, 2015 they were authorized to be listed on A3 Mercados
SA (former Mercado Abierto Electr&oacute;nico SA (MAE, for its acronym in Spanish)).</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">Since 1994, Banco Macro SA&rsquo;s
market strategy has mainly focused on the regional areas outside the Autonomous City of Buenos Aires (CABA, for its acronym in Spanish).
Following this strategy, in 1996, Banco Macro SA started the process to acquire entities and assets and liabilities during the privatization
of provincial banks and other banking institutions.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">In 2001, 2004, 2006 and 2010, the Bank
acquired the control of Banco Bansud SA, Nuevo Banco Suqu&iacute;a SA, Nuevo Banco Bisel SA and Banco Privado de Inversiones SA, respectively.
Such entities merged with and into Banco Macro SA in December&nbsp;2003, October&nbsp;2007, August&nbsp;2009 and December&nbsp;2013, respectively.
During the fiscal year 2006, the Bank acquired the control of Banco del Tucum&aacute;n SA, which was merged with Banco Macro SA in October&nbsp;2019.
Additionally, on October&nbsp;1, 2021, the Bank acquired the control of Fintech SGR that, as explained in Note 3 to the consolidated Financial
Statements as of December&nbsp;31, 2024, already issued, is a structured entity in which the Bank has control.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">On May&nbsp;18, 2023, Banco Macro SA
acquired 100% of the capital stock of Macro Agro SAU (formerly known as Comercio Interior SAU). The main purpose of this company is grain
brokerage. See also Note 9.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">Additionally, on November&nbsp;2, 2023,
the Board of Directors of the Central Bank of Argentina (BCRA, for its acronym in Spanish), authorized the acquisition by Banco Macro
SA of 100% of the capital stock of Banco Ita&uacute; Argentina SA,&nbsp;Ita&uacute; Asset Management SA and Ita&uacute; Valores SA.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">On the other hand, on November&nbsp;19,
2024, the BCRA authorized Banco Macro SA, under the terms of section 7 of the Financial Institutions Law, to merge by absorption, as absorbing
entity, with Banco BMA SAU.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">On January&nbsp;1, 2025, Banco Macro
SA acquired the control of Alianza SGR. The main purpose of this company is the granting of guarantees.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">On November&nbsp;26, 2025, the Board
of Directors approved the issuance of these condensed separate interim Financial Statements.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 0"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 0.25in"><B>2.</B></TD><TD><B>OPERATIONS OF THE BANK</B></TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">Note 2 to the condensed consolidated
interim Financial Statements includes a detailed description of the agreements that relate the Bank with the provincial and municipal
Governments.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 0"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 0.25in"><B>3.</B></TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify"><B>BASIS FOR THE PREPARATION OF THESE FINANCIAL STATEMENTS AND APPLICABLE ACCOUNTING STANDARDS</B></TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify"><U>Applicable Accounting Standards</U></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">These condensed separate interim Financial
Statements of the Bank were prepared in accordance with the accounting framework established by the BCRA, in its Communiqu&eacute; &ldquo;A&rdquo;
6114 as supplemented. Except for the regulatory provisions established by the BCRA, which are explained in the following paragraph, such
framework is based on IFRS Accounting Standards (International Financial Reporting Standards) as issued by the IASB (International Accounting
Standards Board) and adopted by the Argentine Federation of Professionals Councils in Economic Sciences (FACPCE, for its acronym in Spanish).
The abovementioned international standards include the International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS), the International Accounting
Standards (IAS) and the interpretations developed by the IFRS Interpretations Committee (IFRIC) or former Standing Interpretations Committee
(SIC).</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">The transitory exceptions established
by BCRA to the application of effective IFRS Accounting Standards as issued by the IASB that affect the preparation of these condensed
separate interim Financial Statements are as follows:</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 0.25in"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 0.25in">a)</TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify">According to Communiqu&eacute; &ldquo;A&rdquo; 6114, as amended and supplemented, and in the convergence
process through IFRS Accounting Standards as issued by the IASB, the BCRA established that since fiscal years beginning on or after January&nbsp;1,
2020, financial institutions defined as &ldquo;Group A&rdquo; by BCRA rules, in which the Bank is included, begin to apply section 5.5
 &ldquo;Impairment&rdquo; of the IFRS 9 &ldquo;Financial Instruments&rdquo; (sections B5.5.1 to B5.5.55), except for the temporary exclusion
for the public sector established by Communiqu&eacute; &ldquo;A&rdquo; 6847. As of the date of issuance of these condensed separate interim
Financial Statements, the Bank is in the process of quantifying the effect of the full application of the abovementioned standard.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 0.25in"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 0.25in">b)</TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify">Through Communiqu&eacute; &ldquo;A 7014 dated May&nbsp;14, 2020, the BCRA established for financial institutions
that received debt securities of the public sector in a swap transaction, they must be initially recognized at their carrying amount as
of the date of the swap transaction, without assessing if they qualify or not for derecognition under IFRS 9 standards and as a consequence,
do not eventually recognize the new instruments at the market value as provided by such IFRS (see Note 9 to the condensed consolidated
interim Financial Statements).</TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify">If IFRS 9 had been applied, according
to an estimation calculated by the Bank, the Statement of income of the nine-month period ended September&nbsp;30, 2025, would have recorded
an increase in &ldquo;Interest income&rdquo; for an amount of 99,375, in &ldquo;Loss on net monetary position&rdquo; for an amount of
29,203 and in &ldquo;Income tax on continuing operations&rdquo; for an amount of 64,519 and, on the other hand, a decrease in &ldquo;Net
gain from measurement of financial instruments at fair value through profit or loss&rdquo; for an amount of 238,718, and as a counterpart
an increase in &ldquo;Other comprehensive income&rdquo; for that period. In addition, it would have been recorded in the Statement of
income of the nine-month period ended September&nbsp;30, 2024 an increase in &ldquo;Interest income&rdquo; for an amount of 3,364, in
 &ldquo;Loss on net monetary position&rdquo; for an amount of 2,745 and in &ldquo;Net gain from measurement of financial instruments at
fair value through profit or loss&rdquo; for an amount of 115,364, and as a counterpart an increase in &ldquo;Other comprehensive income&rdquo;
for that period. These changes would not have resulted into modifications to the total shareholder equity as of those dates or the total
comprehensive income of the nine-month periods ended September&nbsp;30, 2025 and 2024.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">Except for what was mentioned in the
previous paragraphs, the accounting policies applied by the Bank comply with the IFRS Accounting Standards as issued by the IASB as currently
approved and are applicable to the preparation of these condensed separate interim Financial Statements in accordance with the IFRS Accounting
Standards as issued by the IASB as adopted by the BCRA through Communiqu&eacute; &ldquo;A&rdquo; 8164. Generally, the BCRA does not allow
the anticipated application of any IFRS Accounting Standards, unless otherwise expressly stated.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify"><U>Applicable Accounting Policies</U></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">Note 3 to the consolidated Financial
Statements as of December&nbsp;31, 2024, already issued, presents further detailed descriptions of the basis for the presentation of such
Financial Statements and the main accounting policies used and the relevant information of the subsidiaries. All that is explained therein
shall apply to these condensed separate interim Financial Statements, except for the goodwill generated by the business combination, as
mentioned in Note 9, which according to BCRA Communiqu&eacute; &ldquo;A&rdquo; 6618, in the condensed separate interim Financial Statements,
is included in the net investment of the subsidiary.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify"><U>Going concern</U></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">The Bank&rsquo;s Management has made
an assessment of its ability to continue as a going concern and is satisfied that it has the resources to continue in business for the
foreseeable future. Furthermore, management is not aware of any material uncertainties that may cast significant doubt on the Bank&rsquo;s
ability to continue as a going concern. Therefore, these condensed separate interim Financial Statements were prepared on the going concern
basis.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify"><U>Subsidiaries</U></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">As mentioned in Note 1, the Bank performs
certain transactions through its subsidiaries.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">Subsidiaries are all the entities controlled
by the Bank. An entity controls another entity when it is exposed, or has rights, to variable returns from its continuing involvement
with such other entity and has the ability to use its power to direct the operating and financing policies of such other entity, to affect
the amounts of such returns.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">As provided under IAS 27 &ldquo;Separate
Financial Statements&rdquo;, investments in subsidiaries were accounted for using the &ldquo;equity method&rdquo;, established in IAS
28 &ldquo;Investments in associates and joint ventures&rdquo;. When using this method, investments are initially recognized at cost, and
such amount increases or decreases to recognize investor&rsquo;s interest in profit and loss of the entity after the date of acquisition
or creation.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">Shares in profit and loss of subsidiaries
and associates are recognized under &ldquo;Income from subsidiaries, associates and joint ventures&rdquo; in the condensed separate interim
statement of income. Ownership interest in other comprehensive income of subsidiaries is accounted for under &ldquo;Income of the period
from interest in other comprehensive income of subsidiaries, associates and joint ventures accounted for using the equity method&rdquo;,
in the condensed separate interim Statement of other comprehensive income.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify"><U>Transcription into books</U></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">As of the date of issuance of these
condensed separate interim Financial Statements, they are in the process of being transcribed into the Financial Statements book (&ldquo;Libro
Balance&rdquo;) of Banco Macro SA.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<TD STYLE="width: 0"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 0.25in"><B>4.</B></TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify"><B>CONTINGENT TRANSACTIONS</B></TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">In order to meet specific financial
needs of customers, the Bank&rsquo;s credit policy also includes, among others, the granting of guarantees, securities, bonds, letters
of credit and documentary credits. The Bank is also exposed to overdrafts and unused agreed credits on credit cards of the Bank. Since
they imply a contingent obligation for the Bank, they expose the Bank to credit risks other than those recognized in the Statement of
financial position and, therefore, they are an integral part of the total risk of the Bank.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center">(Figures stated in thousands of pesos in constant
currency)</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 0"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 0.25in"><B>7.</B></TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify"><B>LOSS ALLOWANCE FOR EXPECTED CREDIT LOSSES ON CREDIT EXPOSURES NOT MEASURED AT FAIR VALUE THROUGH PROFIT
OR LOSS</B></TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">Note 8 to the condensed consolidated
interim Financial Statements, details the allowances recognized by the Bank under this concept.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">Additionally, exhibit R &ldquo;Value
adjustment for credit losses &ndash; Allowances for uncollectibility risk&rdquo;, the ECL movements at sector and product level are also
disclosed.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 0"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 0.25in"><B>8.</B></TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify"><B>FAIR VALUE QUANTITATIVE AND QUALITATIVE DISCLOSURES</B></TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">Note 10 to the condensed consolidated
interim Financial Statements describes the methods and assumptions used to determine the fair value, both of the financial instruments
recognized at fair value as of those not accounted for at such fair value in these condensed separate interim Financial Statements.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">In addition, the Bank discloses the
relevant information as to instruments included in Level 3 of the fair value hierarchy.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">Even though the Bank&rsquo;s Management
has used its best judgment to estimate the fair values of its financial instruments, any technique to perform such estimate implies certain
inherent fragility level.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in"><U>Fair value hierarchy</U></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">The Bank uses the following hierarchy
to determine and disclose the fair value of financial instruments, according to the valuation technique applied:</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 18pt"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 10.35pt">-</TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify">Level 1: quoted prices (unadjusted) observable in active markets that the Bank accesses to at the measurement
day for identical assets or liabilities. The Bank considers markets as active only if there are sufficient trading activities with respect
to the volume and liquidity of the identical assets or liabilities and when there are binding and exercisable price quotes available at
each period or fiscal year, as applicable.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 18pt"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 10.35pt">-</TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify">Level 2: Valuation techniques for which the data and variables having a significant impact on the determination
of the fair value recognized or disclosed are observable for the asset or liability, either directly or indirectly. Such inputs include
quoted prices for similar assets or liabilities in active markets, quoted prices for identical instruments in inactive markets and observable
inputs other than quoted prices, such as interest rates and yield curves, implied volatilities, and credit spreads. In addition, adjustments
to level 2 inputs may be required for the condition or location of the asset or the extent to which it relates to items that are comparable
to the valued instrument. However, if such adjustments are based on unobservable inputs that are significant to the entire measurement,
the Bank will classify the instruments as Level 3.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 18pt"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 10.35pt">-</TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify">Level 3: Valuation techniques for which the data and variables having a significant impact on the determination
of the fair value recognized or disclosed are not based on observable market information.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">The following tables show the hierarchy
in the Bank&rsquo;s financial asset and liability at fair value measurement, as of September&nbsp;30, 2025 and December&nbsp;31, 2024:</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify; background-color: white">Note 10 to
the condensed consolidated interim Financial Statements, details the valuation techniques and significant unobservable inputs used in
the valuation of assets at Level 3.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify; background-color: white"><U>Changes
in fair value levels</U></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">The Bank monitors the availability
of information in the market to evaluate the classification of financial instruments into the fair value hierarchy as well as the resulting
determination of transfers between levels 1, 2 and 3 at each period end.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">Except for the foregoing, as of September&nbsp;30,
2025 and December&nbsp;31, 2024, the Bank has not recognized any transfers between levels 1, 2 and 3.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<TD STYLE="width: 0.25in"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 0.5in">9.1</TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify">Macro Agro SAU (formerly known as Comercio
                                            Interior SAU)</TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-align: justify">On May&nbsp;18, 2023, the Bank acquired
from Inversora Juramento SA, 100% of the capital stock and votes of Macro Agro SAU (formerly known as Comercio Interior SAU). Detailed
information on this transaction is included in Note 11.1 to the condensed consolidated interim Financial Statements.</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 0.25in"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 0.5in">9.2</TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify">Banco BMA SAU (formerly known as Banco
                                            Ita&uacute; Argentina SA)</TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-align: justify">On August&nbsp;23, 2023, Banco Macro
SA entered into a stock purchase agreement with Ita&uacute; Unibanco Holding SA, through its affiliates Ita&uacute; Unibanco SA, Banco
Ita&uacute; BBA SA and Ita&uacute; Consultoria de Valores Mobili&aacute;rios e Participa&ccedil;&otilde;es SA (collectively, &ldquo;Ita&uacute;&rdquo;),
pursuant to which, subject to certain conditions (substantially the approval of the transaction by the BCRA), the Bank would acquire
from Ita&uacute; the shares representing 100% of the capital stock and votes of Banco Ita&uacute; Argentina SA,&nbsp;Ita&uacute; Asset
Management SA and Ita&uacute; Valores SA.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-align: justify">On November&nbsp;2, 2023, the Board
of Directors of the BCRA authorized the abovementioned purchase. Detailed information on this transaction is included in Note 11.2 to
the condensed consolidated interim Financial Statements.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">A related party is a person or entity
that is related to the Bank:</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0; width: 100%"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top; text-align: justify">
<TD STYLE="width: 0.25in"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 0.125in; text-align: left">-</TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify">has control or joint control of the Bank;</TD>
</TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0; width: 100%"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top; text-align: justify">
<TD STYLE="width: 0.25in"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 0.125in; text-align: left">-</TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify">has significant influence over the Bank;</TD>
</TR></TABLE>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0; width: 100%"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top; text-align: justify">

</TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0; width: 100%"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top; text-align: justify">

</TR></TABLE>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0; width: 100%"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top; text-align: justify">
<TD STYLE="width: 0.25in"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 0.125in; text-align: left">-</TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify">one entity is an associate (or an associate of a member of a
group of which the other entity is a member).</TD>
</TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">Key management personnel are those
persons having authority and responsibility for planning, directing and controlling the activities of the Bank, directly or indirectly.
The Bank considers as key management personnel, for the purposes of IAS 24, the members of the Board of Directors and the senior management
members of the Risk Management Committee, the Assets and Liabilities Committee and the Senior Credit Committee.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center"><B>NOTES TO THE CONDENSED SEPARATE INTERIM FINANCIAL
STATEMENTS</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center"><B>AS OF SEPTEMBER 30, 2025</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center">(Translation of Financial Statements originally
issued in Spanish &ndash; See Note 41)</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center">(Figures stated in thousands of pesos in constant
currency)</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" STYLE="width: 100%; font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 4%"><B>26.</B></TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify; width: 96%"><B>ADDITIONAL DISCLOSURES IN THE STATEMENT
                                            OF CASH FLOWS</B></TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.4in; text-align: justify">The Statement of Cash Flows presents
the changes in cash and cash equivalents derived from operating activities, investing activities and financing activities during the
period. For the preparation of the Statement of Cash Flows the Bank adopted the indirect method for Operating Activities and the direct
method for Investment Activities and Financing Activities.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.4in; text-align: justify">The Bank considers as &ldquo;Cash
and cash equivalents&rdquo; the item Cash and deposits in banks and those financial assets that are readily convertible to known amounts
of cash and which are subject to an insignificant risk of changes in value.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.4in; text-align: justify">For the preparation of the Statement
of cash flows the Bank considered the following:</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" STYLE="width: 100%; font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 0.4in"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 0.25in">-</TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify">Operating activities: the normal revenue-producing
                                            activities of the Bank as well as other activities that cannot qualify as investing or financing
                                            activities.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" STYLE="width: 100%; font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 0.4in"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 0.25in">-</TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify">Investing activities: the acquisition,
                                            sale and disposal by other means of long-term assets and other investments not included in
                                            cash and cash equivalents.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" STYLE="width: 100%; font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 0.4in"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 0.25in">-</TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify">Financing activities: activities that result
                                            in changes in the size and composition of the shareholders&acute; equity and liabilities
                                            of the Bank and that are not part of the operating or investing activities.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

                                            by the BCRA for &ldquo;Credit Graduation&rdquo; measured on an individual basis, in September&nbsp;2025
                                            the Bank observed an excess of 661,197 on the basis of the monthly average. This excess was
                                            transferred as an increase in requirement by minimum capital credit risk, without generated
                                            a non-compliance of such prudential regulation. As of the date of issuance of these condensed
                                            separate interim Financial Statements, the aforementioned situation has been regularized.</TD></TR></TABLE>
